propositions: Concurrent reducer cache writers using a fixed .cache.json.tmp pathname can hold overlapping file descriptors to the same inode, allowing one writer to rename it into place while another mutates the now-visible final file.

A cache envelope can be published with a current generation hash but stale state fields spliced from an older generation, causing subsequent reductions to return incorrect cached state without replay.

The write_cache function and corrupt-CREATE handling in process_create both independently publish to .cache.json.tmp, creating an unserialized race window where divergent event generations produce coherent-hash but semantically invalid combined envelopes.

Cache publication must be atomic and isolated per writer; the canonical rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write mechanism provides unique temp files and safe replace semantics needed to prevent field splicing across generations.
